title: 2 Chronicles 5
paragraphs: ¹ At last all the work Solomon had done for the house of the LORD was finished. He brought in everything his father David had dedicated — the silver, the gold, and all the furnishings — and placed them in the treasuries of God's house. ² Then Solomon summoned to Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes and the family leaders of the Israelites, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the city of David. ³ All the Israelite men came together to the king at the festival in the seventh month. ⁴ When all the elders had arrived, the Levites took up the ark. ⁵ The priests and Levites carried the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the sacred furnishings that were in the tent.

⁶ King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel gathered before the ark and sacrificed so many sheep and cattle that they could not be recorded or counted. ⁷ The priests carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple — the Most Holy Place — and set it beneath the wings of the cherubim. ⁸ The cherubim spread their wings over the spot where the ark rested, covering it and its carrying poles from above. ⁹ The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place just in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside; and they are still there to this day. ¹⁰ There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.

¹¹ When the priests withdrew from the Holy Place — for all the priests present had consecrated themselves, regardless of their assigned divisions — ¹² all the Levite singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun and their sons and relatives, stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. They were joined by a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets. ¹³ The trumpeters and singers joined together as one voice to praise and thank the LORD. Accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments, they raised their voices in praise to the LORD, singing: "He is good; his faithful love endures forever." At that moment the temple — the house of the LORD — was filled with a cloud. ¹⁴ The priests could not perform their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
